runs.note: Run over every Part by Claude (agent), for Legalese, 5 Oct 2026; the Interpretation Act 1984 provisions bearing on each Part read first (ss 5, 16, 18, 19, 32, 37, 61, 62, 74). Listed the s 3 terms the scope uses (approved form, expiry day, lessor, party, pet, rent, residential premises, residential tenancy agreement, security bond, tenancy, tenancy period, tenant) and the operative terms left undefined (term, renewal, continuation, method and means, r 12I 'authorised notice'), and checked each use against its definition. Part I: 'tenancy' and 'tenancy period' (U-11, U-12), 'lessor' (U-10), 'party' para (a)(ii)-(iii) against s 31B(3)(b) (L-07). Part IV Division 1: 'renewal' in two models (U-02), 'method' and 'means', and 'notice of increase' for a notice under s 31A (D-42), 'term' (U-09). Part V: 'term' (U-09). Part VI: 'authorised notice' against s 85's 'required or authorised to be given' (U-17). Part 7: 'commencement' is defined identically in ss 99(1) and 100(1) (no candidate). Regulations: r 12I (U-17). Checked and not recorded: 'expiry day ... or the happening of an event' with s 70A(3) (an expiry fixed by an event gets 30 days' notice after the event is known, which protects the tenant); 'possession' in s 60(1)(b)(i) against 'vacant possession' in (a)(i) and (g) (different routes; no outcome found to turn on it).

Run over every Part, 5 Oct 2026. Every entry in the reference register checked against the pinned print: every target exists at 07-a0-00, and REF-41 (29 July 2024) agrees with SL 2024/143 cl 2(f). Encoded references called with the citing provision's facts: the note to s 31B(2) pointing to s 76C (U-08); s 3A(2) and s 26A's 'the residential tenancy agreement' where two agreements between the same parties are in force (L-04); s 31(1C), (2) against s 29(1)(b), (2) (not recorded: s 31(2) caps a bond increase at 4 weeks' rent even above the r 11 threshold at which s 29(2) lifts the cap on the first bond, an asymmetry not shown to produce a wrong result); s 85 for every in-scope notice (U-17); s 65 against s 32 (T-33); the note to s 64(3) against s 26B (consistent); r 5CB's amending words applied to s 31(1A) and (1B)(b) (each applies exactly once). Antecedents: 'the tenancy' in s 30(1)(b) (U-11, U-12), 'the term' in s 31B(2)(c) (U-08, U-09), 'the person who applied' in s 32(5) (U-15). Outside the encoded Parts and noted only: s 103(1) defines 'regulation 12BA' as 'the Residential Tenancies Regulations 1989 section 12BA'.

Run over every Part, 5 Oct 2026. Step 1, each regulation in scope against its empowering provision: s 6 for rr 5B, 5CA, 5CB, 7D, 7F and 7FA; s 85(1)(c) and s 88 for r 12I; ss 27(2)(a), 29(1)(b)(ii) and 29(2) for rr 10AD, 10A and 11. Regulation 5CB modifies s 31 for all premises under s 6(b) (P-31); r 5B's effect on s 31 (I-30). The others are within their powers on their face. Step 2, powers conferred in the encoded Parts: the lessor's to increase the rent (s 30) and change the method (s 31A), with no limit on amount, s 32 being the check (no candidate); the court's under ss 26B(4), 32(4), 64(4), 65(2) and 76C(3), each with a stated test; the Commissioner's to approve forms (s 88C, outside scope, a fact). Step 3, options opened and not closed: none found.

Run over every Part, 5 Oct 2026. Each duty paired with its consequence: ss 27(1), 27AA(1), (3), 28(1), (2), 29(1)(b), 32(7) and 82(2) carry penalties; the closing words of ss 30(1) and 31A(1), and s 31(1), carry none (E-32); s 70A(3) states none (U-27); s 26A has a civil remedy (s 26B) by design. Offences: a penalty for each; proceedings within 2 years (s 87, outside the encoded Parts); s 82(2) against renewals made to avoid the limit (E-16). Defences and exemptions: s 27AA(2) (a sign stating no amount) covers only signs and does not swallow the offence; r 7F's exemption from s 82 is confined to sub-letting agreements. An order under s 32(4) from an earlier day has no machinery for the excess already paid (E-38).

Run over every Part, 5 Oct 2026, applied to the amendments that made the in-scope text: the Residential Tenancies Amendment Act 2024 ss 4, 17, 21-28, 34 and 55 set against the compilation (every instruction applies exactly once), and the replaced s 31B set against the former s 31B (Residential Tenancies Amendment Act 2011 s 28). Step 2, provisions that depend on what was amended: the former s 31B's 30-day rule for a renegotiated lease was removed with nothing in its place for a rise made by the new agreement (M-01); s 99 continues s 30 but not s 31A (M-21); the change from 'a form approved by the Minister' to 'the approved form' and ss 99-100 (M-20). Step 3, things done under the old law: notices given before 29 July 2024 (U-22, M-20, M-21), increases under the former s 30 (U-23), fixed terms within s 99 (U-19). Step 4, the purpose stated in the extrinsic material tested from commencement: the 12-month limit across consecutive agreements (M-01, L-03, L-05, L-06). Not recorded: agreements renegotiated before 29 July 2024 under the former s 31B's 30-day rule (spent by the end of August 2024).
